strictFailureAnalysis.x64Baseline: Compiler-default plain execution passes, but the suspended baseline refuses at kernel-image-validity with errno13/signing error-67062. No mutation was attempted, no payload marker appeared, and the original was reaped with signal9. That baseline termination is not the successful-mutation branch required of after-check/writer-open. The surfaced Node assertion is13!==0 at native.ts:476.
strictFailureAnalysis.arm64Baseline: Compiler-default baseline reaches an observed/matched image and runs A normally, with flags570556417. This is a baseline control; it does not repair either later ad-hoc mutation case.
strictFailureAnalysis.bothSignedFailures: Both after-check and writer-open record stopped-before-user and zero pre-gate markers, original/kernel device+inode equality and expected A digest, imageMatched=true, then mutation errno0, one resume, LIB/BIN:A/MAIN:A and exit0/signal0. They are INCOMPLETE under the unchanged strict successful-write oracle. Actual ETXTBSY was not observed in these four cases.

strictFailureAnalysis.preGateControls: Rename substitution produces a different kernel inode and replacement-B hash; in-place pre-gate mutation retains the inode but yields replacement-B hash. Both are rejected before resume with zero markers/signal9. They establish the sampled pre-gate rejection behavior, not continuous post-gate byte custody.
strictFailureAnalysis.scriptNegative: The plain script emits SCRIPT:A. The explicit script-negative case records a distinct kernel executable image, writes successfully and emits SCRIPT:B, so COUNTEREXAMPLE remains correct and scriptQualified stays false. This is an intentional negative-control classification, not an extra hidden native pass or an unexplained third failing job step.

strictFailureAnalysis.flags: All four signed after-check/writer-open cases still show570425345 (0x22000001). The retained earlier advisory establishes that absence/presence of hard/kill flags alone does not prove the missing continuous guard. No flag-setting fix is inferred.
